answer: The jade bond is the main Sybil brake: every identity must lock collateral worth more than one epoch can pay out, and payouts track verified work rather than headcount. Splitting one operator into a thousand personas needs a thousand separate stakes while earnings stay flat, so each clone is deadweight loss. A juniper reputation layer compounds this, because slashed history is public across venues, so fresh keys pay full warm-up cost again. A karst scarcity ledger also caps claims per window, excluding extra Sybils by scarcity instead of flagging them later.
